Title: NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
Description:
We built NariQ: 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B that retain near-BF16 quality across agentic tasks, math, multilingual reasoning, and image understanding.

To our knowledge, this is the first 3-bit-or-lower quantization that retains BF16 lvl performance on long-horizon agentic tasks.

Benchmarks (BF16 / 3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit):

- DeepSWE: 39.8 / 41.0 / 41.9 / 28.6

- Terminal-Bench 2.1: 62.6 / 63.8 / 60.2 / 52.4

- AIME 25+26: 97.7

Title: Show HN: Type-C – variants, options, generics and pattern matching for C
Description:
I love C, but often using it for parsing, tree walking or complex error handling leads to spaghetti code.

Of course there is Swift, Ocaml or Rust for situations like that, but then you are either forced to convert the entire codebase, or add a runtime library or go through the pain of bridging C to the new language. Sometimes there are no compilers for the target architecture too when you are working on embedded stuff.
